title: Philips FMV Demonstration Disc multilingual stream switch
symptom: Switching the running Multilingual sample from Dutch to Japanese records one MP2 decode error
expected: The native in-place audio-stream change continues cleanly without decoder errors or underflow

hypotheses.hardware_explanation: The FMA stream selector changes at a PES boundary which need not be a Layer-II frame boundary; the host decoder currently treats expected acquisition of the new stream as loss of synchronization.
supporting_evidence: Philips multilingual.c changes only ma_cntrl stream selection during uninterrupted playback.
The FMA register changes from stream 0 to 2 while audio and video decoding continue.
The run records one audio error and 54 resynchronization bytes, with zero demux/video errors.
contradicting_evidence: Discarding the old compressed tail removes the decode error but creates repeated audio underflows, so the correct FIFO boundary is not yet established.
hypotheses.falsifying_test: Capture the compressed audio queue and PES boundaries immediately before and after ma_cntrl. If the new selected stream begins on a complete MP2 frame and no old bytes remain, the error originates inside frame decoding rather than selection-boundary handling.

experiments.strategy: Count the native FMA stream change and require both decoders to advance afterward with zero cumulative errors.
assumptions: The Japanese button maps to FMA stream 2 as shown by Philips source and the live register.
experiments.expected: Audio/video continue and cumulative errors remain zero.
experiments.actual: FMA stream changed from 0 to 2; video and audio continued to 985/1,498 decoded frames, but audio accumulated one error and 54 resync bytes.
improvements: The stream switch is now a deterministic, payload-free title gate.
experiments.evidence_quality: high: direct Philips sample source and bounded native-title diagnostics

conditions: VMPEG in-place FMA audio-stream selection during playback
invalidated_by: Changes to FMA stream selection, MPEG demux, MP2 FIFO ownership, or decoder error accounting
repeat_when: Any invalidating dependency changes or a packet-boundary trace becomes available

context.scenario: clear undecoded audio bytes and reset frame state on FMA stream change

experiments.strategy: Discard compressed old-stream tail while preserving decoded PCM.
assumptions: Old compressed bytes must not prefix the newly selected stream.
experiments.expected: No MP2 error and no audible transport interruption.
experiments.actual: The MP2 error disappeared, but the run accumulated 58 audio underflows and 619 sync-acquisition bytes.
regressions: Repeated audio underflow after the stream selection
experiments.evidence_quality: medium: deterministic title run, but no packet-boundary capture

conditions: The compressed FIFO is cleared immediately on the FMA register write
invalidated_by: Evidence locating the actual hardware stream-selection boundary
repeat_when: A trace identifies which bytes hardware retains or discards

context.scenario: retain compressed/PCM queues but reset Layer-II synchronization state

experiments.strategy: Treat the switch as expected sync acquisition without changing buffered bytes.
assumptions: The error is solely the synchronized flag classifying skipped bytes.
experiments.expected: The 54 skipped bytes become acquisition bytes and the error count stays zero.
experiments.actual: The same one MP2 error remained, showing the failure occurs after the immediate register write rather than only in its existing synchronization flag.
experiments.evidence_quality: medium: deterministic title run without byte-boundary capture

conditions: Only decoder state is reset at the FMA stream-register write
invalidated_by: Changes to PES delivery timing or a later proven switch boundary
repeat_when: The reset can be moved to a proven packet/frame boundary
